misconceptions.description: Believing a published site needs no ongoing attention, ignoring that content goes stale and links break over time
misconceptions.trigger: learner treats launch as the end of work and plans no recurring upkeep
misconceptions.feedback: A live site decays: resumes age and links break. Plan small recurring upkeep, not a one-time launch or an unrealistic weekly redesign.

misconceptions.description: Assuming internal links stay valid forever even after files are renamed or moved
misconceptions.trigger: learner renames a file and does not re-check the links that pointed to it
misconceptions.feedback: Renaming or moving a file breaks every link to it. Schedule a periodic link check so broken paths surface before visitors hit a 404.

misconceptions.description: Applying a generic AI maintenance checklist (SSL renewal, server patching) to a static GitHub Pages site that does not have those components
misconceptions.trigger: learner keeps server-oriented tasks that do not apply to a static host
misconceptions.feedback: GitHub Pages manages HTTPS and runs no server you patch. Strip checklist items that assume a server and keep the content and link checks that fit a static site.

misconceptions.description: Recording vague intentions like keep it updated as a maintenance plan instead of specific triggers and tasks
misconceptions.trigger: learner writes update sometime with no cadence or concrete actions
misconceptions.feedback: Name the trigger and the exact tasks: on the first of each quarter, swap the oldest project, refresh the resume, click every link. Vague intent cannot be repeated.
